issues: (1) No attempt to get around the measurement. The diff only changes the final validity-repair step: it clips centers to [0,1], then loops to shrink any radius that crosses a wall or overlaps another circle, then subtracts 1e-15 as a safety margin. There is no file or network access and no pasted coordinates.

(2) No bug that makes the result meaningless. Minor risk: the loop stops after 100 passes even if overlaps remain, and when a radius is floored at 0 the other circle only gets half the shrink it needs. Both are unlikely to matter, and the harness check would turn any leftover overlap into a crash rather than a fake score. Clipping centers can move a circle, but its radius is then reduced to fit, so validity holds. The diff doesn't show where sum_radii is computed. It needs to be recomputed from the repaired radii, as presumably happens downstream.

(3) The numbers match the decision. Candidate -2.636 (1 run) against incumbent -2.6360 (1 run) is no measurable gain. That is expected: this is a cleanup of the validity margin, with a gain of about 1e-10 at most. Rejecting is consistent with that.

z can't be recomputed properly: with one run per arm there is no variance estimate, and the values agree to the 4 decimals shown. The reported z = 0.002 is effectively zero and doesn't conflict with the numbers.
